newsitem.title: USA: Sour crudes slide in weaker U.S. Gulf cash sector.
newsitem.headline: Sour crudes slide in weaker U.S. Gulf cash sector.

text.p: Sour crude grade barrels marked sharp losses Monday in the U.S. Gulf, pressured by an overdrawn market and fears of plentiful alternative supply.

"There is talk of much more Canadian crude coming down," said a trader. West Texas Sour/Midland collapsed all the way to a $1.45 discount against August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, some 20 cents weaker than late Friday.
August WTI/Cushing talked late at $19.15-25 a barrel, 10 cents weaker than Friday's close.
August/September WTI widened all session to a 24 cents deficit in favor of the second month. August futures expire on Tuesday, leaving paper dealings in a state of flux.
Cash markets held steady from the morning, but continued to display bearish trends, notably for sours.
Sweet barrels featured Midland/WTI barrels selling last at 30 cents under the marker, after moving at 26 cts and 24 cts below level. Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire easing to a 30 cents discount.

Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold between 20-23 cents over the August benchmark, steady from Friday. Arbitrage clockings for Brent-WTI underpinned the U.S. grade, leaving some refiners to consider bringing over Brent barrels.
A U.S. refiner was reportedly thinking of loading a Brent cargo for September 5-10 delivery to the U.S. Gulf, talking prices at August WTI -25 cents.
Outright crudes were mostly pressured by news Iraq formally sent its aid distribution plan to New York for approval by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.

Iraqi Ambassador to the United Nations Nizar Hamdoon is scheduled to formally hand the plan to Annan Tuesday at 1100 EDT. Annan needs to sign off on the aid plan in order to further implement the stalled "oil-for-food" accord.

After the aid plan is set, the submission of a new pricing formula for second round oil contracts is needed. The Iraqis were given approval from June 8 to sell $2 billion of oil, as an extension of the oil for aid accord.
However, Iraq wanted an aid plan in place before renewed liftings started, and now have a more narrow timeframe to sell the oil share.
